_comment: Places where change is visible from space, one per event. imagery_timeline.py finds every distinct Esri World Imagery Wayback capture here. zoom = map zoom used for the comparison.

central-valley.label: Tulare Lake bed, near Corcoran
central-valley.note: Dry farmland inside the sinking bowl, plus the old Tulare Lake bed that the 2023 storms flooded again.

norfolk.label: Downtown Norfolk waterfront
norfolk.note: The Elizabeth River waterfront, where sinking ground and rising sea bring the most frequent tidal flooding.

jakarta.label: North Jakarta coast
jakarta.note: Reclaimed islands and new sea walls, built along a coast that is sinking faster than the sea is rising.

mexico-city.label: Former Lake Texcoco
mexico-city.note: A new airport was started here in 2015 and cancelled in 2018. It sat on the same soft lakebed clay that makes the city sink.

svartsengi.label: Grindavík and the Sundhnúkur craters
svartsengi.note: Barrier walls and fresh lava from the eruptions since December 2023, at the edge of Grindavík.

kilauea.label: Kapoho, lower East Rift Zone
kilauea.note: The 2018 eruption buried this bay and neighbourhood under new land.

san-andreas.label: The creeping fault trace
san-andreas.note: Creep here is a few centimetres a year. You can't see that in photos, and that's exactly why radar matters.

campi-flegrei.label: Pozzuoli harbour
campi-flegrei.note: The ground under this harbour has risen more than a metre since 2005.

kahramanmaras.label: Antakya city centre
kahramanmaras.note: About 200 km south-west of the epicentre: whole blocks collapsed in the 6 February 2023 earthquakes.

nile-delta.label: New Mansoura, on the delta coast
nile-delta.note: A whole new city has gone up on this low, flat coast since 2017. Nearby, the land sinks a few millimetres a year while the sea rises about 3.4 mm a year.
